citation.authors: Goyal M, Singh S, Sibinga EM, Gould NF et al

record.population: 47 trials, 3,515 participants in diverse adult clinical populations
record.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of meditation programmes against active controls
record.finding: Mindfulness meditation programmes had moderate evidence of improved anxiety (effect size 0.38 at 8 weeks), depression (0.30) and pain (0.33), and low evidence of improved stress and mental-health quality of life. Low or insufficient evidence for positive mood, attention, substance use, eating habits, sleep and weight. No evidence that meditation programmes were better than any active treatment (drugs, exercise, other behavioural therapies).
